Reading what an identifier knows

Source: vignettes/articles/fields.Rmd
fields.Rmd
library(zuid)

An identifier is a value with a structure. A version 7 UUID begins with a millisecond time, a KSUID with a second count from its own epoch, and a Snowflake packs a time, a node and a sequence into one 64-bit integer. This article shows how zuid finds out which format a string is, how strictly it checks it, and what it reads from it.

Which format is it?

id_detect() tries the structured formats, those whose text proves its own format: UUID, ULID, TypeID, UPID, SCRU128, SCRU64, KSUID, XID, ObjectId and CID. It returns one format per element, or NA:

ids <- c(
  "018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3",
  "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav",
  "9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g",
  "not an identifier"
)
found <- id_detect(ids)
as.vector(found)
#> [1] "uuid" "ulid" NA     "xid"  NA

NA means two different things, and the candidates attribute tells them apart. The last string fits no format. The third fits two: a ULID in lowercase, or a TypeID without a prefix. zuid does not pick one.

attr(found, "candidates")[3:5]
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "ulid"   "typeid"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "xid"
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> character(0)

A hint restricts the formats tried. It settles an ambiguity, and it is the only way to detect a format whose text proves nothing, such as a NanoID, which is any string over its alphabet:

as.vector(id_detect("01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav", hint = "typeid"))
#> [1] "typeid"
as.vector(id_detect("V1StGXR8_Z5jdHi6B-myT", hint = "nanoid"))
#> [1] "nanoid"

id_parse() without a format detects one format for the whole vector. When the vector is ambiguous, or holds more than one format, it raises an error rather than guess. The error’s class says which:

err <- tryCatch(id_parse(ids[3]), error = identity)
class(err)
#> [1] "zuid_ambiguous_error" "zuid_error"           "error"               
#> [4] "condition"
err$candidates
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "ulid"   "typeid"

How strict?

id_valid() and id_parse() check at one of three levels, each including the one before:

  • "syntax": the alphabet, the length, the case and the separators.
  • "structure", the default: the value’s own rules. For a UUID, the variant bits.
  • "strict": the value is one its specification defines. For a UUID, a version from 1 to 8, and a time no later than now plus a tolerance.

The second UUID below has the wrong variant bits. It is well-formed text, but it is not an RFC 9562 UUID:

x <- c(
  "018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3",
  "018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-cc5d-6e7f8091a2b3"
)
id_valid(x, "uuid", level = "syntax")
#> [1] TRUE TRUE
id_valid(x, "uuid")
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE

Inspection never raises on input. Text that fails the level is NA in a parsed vector, unless strict = TRUE asks for an error:

id_parse(c(x, "nope"), "uuid")
#> <zuid_uuid[3]>
#> [1] 018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3 <NA>                                
#> [3] <NA>
err <- tryCatch(id_parse("nope", "uuid", strict = TRUE), error = identity)
class(err)
#> [1] "zuid_parse_error" "zuid_error"       "error"            "condition"

A UUID can arrive in other text forms. form names the one to read:

id_parse("{018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3}", "uuid", form = "braced")
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3
id_parse("urn:uuid:018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3", "uuid", form = "urn")
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3

Fields

id_fields() returns a data frame with one row per element and the same columns for every format. A column a format does not have is NA:

v1 <- id_parse("c232ab00-9414-11ec-b3c8-9f6bdeced846", "uuid")
id_fields(v1)[c("version", "time", "time_unit", "node", "sequence")]
#>   version                time time_unit         node sequence
#> 1       1 2022-02-22 19:22:22     100ns 9f6bdeced846    13256

A version 1 UUID records its time in 100-nanosecond ticks since 1582, a node and a clock sequence. A version 7 records milliseconds since 1970 and random bits:

v7 <- id_parse("018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3", "uuid")
id_fields(v7)[c("version", "time", "time_unit", "random")]
#>   version                time time_unit              random
#> 1       7 2024-05-12 04:42:39        ms 292cc5d6e7f8091a2b3

Other formats fill the columns they have. An XID has a machine, a process and a counter; a TypeID has a prefix; a CID has a codec, a hash function and a digest:

xid <- id_parse("9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g", "xid")
id_fields(xid)[c("time", "node", "process", "sequence")]
#>                  time   node process sequence
#> 1 2011-03-22 17:50:19 60f486   58408  4271561

tid <- id_parse("user_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q", "typeid")
id_fields(tid)[c("prefix", "time", "version")]
#>   prefix                time version
#> 1   user 2023-06-30 03:34:18       7

cid <- id_parse(
  "bafybeigdyrzt5sfp7udm7hu76uh7y26nf3efuylqabf3oclgtqy55fbzdi",
  "cid"
)
id_fields(cid)[c("version", "codec", "hash")]
#>   version  codec     hash
#> 1       1 dag-pb sha2-256

id_formats() lists each format’s width, alphabet, time unit and epoch.

Time

id_time() reads the creation time as a POSIXct, or as milliseconds since 1970 with class = "ms". Each format has its own resolution and epoch, and zuid converts from them:

id_time(v1)
#> [1] "2022-02-22 19:22:22 UTC"
id_time(id_parse("0ujtsYcgvSTl8PAuAdqWYSMnLOv", "ksuid"))
#> [1] "2017-10-10 04:00:47 UTC"
ms <- id_time(id_parse("01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "ulid"), class = "ms")
format(ms, scientific = FALSE)
#> [1] "1469922850259"

A format with no time, such as a version 4 UUID or a NanoID, gives NA.

Snowflakes need a layout

A Snowflake is a decimal integer whose bits each platform divides in its own way, from its own epoch. The digits alone say nothing about which platform made them, so zuid reads a Snowflake only under a layout. id_layout() has Twitter’s, Discord’s, Instagram’s and Sonyflake’s, and builds custom ones:

discord <- id_layout("discord")
discord
#> <zuid_layout discord>
#> | time 42 | worker 5 | process 5 | sequence 12 |
#> time: ms units from 2015-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
s <- id_parse("175928847299117063", "snowflake", layout = discord)
id_fields(s)[c("time", "node", "sequence")]
#>                  time               node sequence
#> 1 2016-04-30 11:18:25 worker=1,process=0        7

The layout travels with the vector, so id_time() and id_fields() need it only once. Under another layout the same digits give another time:

id_time(s)
#> [1] "2016-04-30 11:18:25 UTC"
id_time(id_parse("175928847299117063", "snowflake", layout = id_layout("twitter")))
#> [1] "2012-03-03 13:01:20 UTC"
